props.title: Get Rich or Die Tryin'
props.initialSlug: 50 Cent's raw journey from dealer to rap stardom

sections.content: Get Rich or Die Tryin' (2005) marks 50 Cent's semi-autobiographical film debut, following the template of 8 Mile (2002) but with grittier street elements. Director Jim Sheridan, known for In the Name of the Father (1993), brings surprising emotional depth to this story of an orphaned drug dealer pursuing rap stardom. While the film received mixed reviews, it captures the raw energy of early 2000s hip-hop cinema alongside contemporaries like Hustle & Flow (2005).

sections.content: The mid-2000s saw a wave of hip-hop films exploring the intersection of music and street life. ATL (2006) took a lighter approach focusing on coming-of-age themes, while Notorious (2009) dove deep into the East Coast-West Coast rivalry. These films shared common threads about escape through artistic expression and the struggle between street credibility and mainstream success. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Hip-Hop Cinema

The groundwork for films like Get Rich was laid by earlier classics like Krush Groove (1985) and Beat Street (1984), which documented hip-hop culture's emergence. By the 2000s, the genre evolved to include more complex narratives about the music industry itself, seen in films like Brown Sugar (2002) and Save the Last Dance (2001), though often sacrificing authenticity for commercial appeal.
